\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{محل} (mahal)}{محل (mahal)}]{\ur{محل} (mahal) — a palace}

\label{lesson:UR-C101-mahal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a market, then the Urdu for a police station.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{محل}}
\textbf{\ur{محل}} — \emph{mahal} — \textquotedblleft{}a palace\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{محل}} (\emph{mahal}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{maḥall}, \textquotedblleft{}a place of alighting, a quarter\textquotedblright{}, which reached Urdu through Persian. Its Arabic root is \emph{ḥ-l-l} (Lane). In Urdu it came to mean \textquotedblleft{}a palace\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mahal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mahal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{mahal}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a market, then the Urdu for a police station, then say \emph{mahal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{محل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A palace\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دروازہ} (darvāzā)}{دروازہ (darvāzā)}]{\ur{دروازہ} (darvāzā) — a door}

\label{lesson:UR-C101-darvaza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a cinema, then the Urdu for a field.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دروازہ}}
\textbf{\ur{دروازہ}} — \emph{darvāzā} — \textquotedblleft{}a door\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دروازہ}} (\emph{darvāzā}) is a loan, usually traced to Persian \emph{darvāza}, \textquotedblleft{}gate, door\textquotedblright{}. Its first part, Persian \emph{dar}, \textquotedblleft{}door\textquotedblright{}, goes back to the same ancient root as English \emph{door} and Sanskrit \emph{dvāra}.
\end{cousinweb}
